newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Yorks Elec eyes benefits this year.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Yorks Elec eyes benefits this year.

text.p: British regional electricity company (Rec) Yorkshire Electricity Group Plc expects to implement a return of value to shareholders by the end of the current financial year, chief executive Malcolm Chatwin said.
"We hope to do something by way of a return of value to shareholders within this financial year," he told Reuters in a telephone interview on Tuesday.
The company said in a statement with half year results that it intended to return further value to shareholders after hiking its interim dividend by 33 percent to 15.8 pence per share.
Pretax profits for the six months slipped to 80.8 million stg from 110.6 million stg previously as a pricing review earlier this year took effect.
Yorkshire, which is one of only three remaining independent and currently unpursued Recs, has had "no serious bid approaches", Chatwin said, and was "happy being independent."

He said there had been no discussions with fellow Rec Northern Electric, which said on Tuesday it planned to merge its supply business with another Rec as part of a defence against a 650 pence per share bid from CE Electric, which is 70 percent-owned by CalEnergy of the U.S..
Northern "have not spoken to us about it," Chatwin said.
He added that there were no plans for increased cooperation with the company's counterpart in water, Yorkshire Water, over existing projects.
"At the current time there are no plans to do anything further," Chatwin said.
He said half year profits were "generally speaking indicative" of the likely full year performance with a couple of upsides such as property disposals.
Costs were likely to be "level pegging", he added, with investment in information technology and staff training ahead of liberalisation of the market in 1998 offsetting any savings.
